**Trump–Xi White House summit (24 Sep) — 'long on friendship, short on commitments' (Alhurra): no Hormuz text, no buyer-sanctions carve-out, no pressure commitment; trigger resolved 'no commitment'.** Xinhua: Xi backs a return to the 17-Jun Islamabad MoU and renewed US–Iran talks. US Amb. Perdue claims 'assurances' (Fox) — CLAIMED; a senior Iranian official told Reuters China assured Tehran it would not restrict ties — CLAIMED. Trade truce extended 10 Nov → 10 Jan 2027 (Bessent, 23 Sep); advanced-chip controls excluded. China remains the only buyer of a supply that fell to zero in September; Mahan Air landed in Guangzhou after the 23-Sep airline ban (China calls the sanctions 'illegal'). China MFA (Mao Ning, 12 Oct) condemned Houthi attacks on Saudi airports, urged dialogue. Chinese CXMT memory announcement hit global memory stocks (12–13 Oct). Pre-Golden Week mini-stimulus + ¥550bn provincial bond quota (9 Oct). — mixed tags.

**Beijing confirmed Xi Jinping's state visit to Washington 23–25 Sep (Bloomberg/Reuters 21 Sep) — first US visit in ~3 years; Iran/Hormuz and secondary sanctions on Iran's buyers on the agenda alongside rare earths/AI; state dinner Thu with Huang/Altman/Nadella (Yahoo).** Wang Yi to Araghchi in Beijing (19 Sep): China 'willing to cooperate with Iran' and urged 'the opening of the Strait of Hormuz at an early date' plus resumed US–Iran negotiations — Beijing asking Tehran in public to open the strait is a shift in emphasis. Markets traded the trade leg: Nasdaq record, SMH +4%, copper +2.1%, KOSPI >7,000. (Bloomberg; Reuters via Just Security; Fox live 19 Sep; Yahoo Finance) — CONFIRMED.

**Araghchi in Beijing (16 Sep): the June memorandum 'remains in force'; 'Iran has already agreed with Oman on a plan to reopen the Strait of Hormuz' (Chinese readout/TASS). Wang Yi: China 'ready to strengthen dialogue and cooperation with the Iranian side.'** No new Chinese commitment; Kpler: ~29mb of Iranian crude afloat outside the blockade — China is the only buyer that matters for it. (TASS; CNBC; oprep) — visit CONFIRMED / statements REPORTED; RHETORIC.

China is the named non-exempt target of 'Operation Economic Outcast' (Bessent 24 Aug: China historically ~90% of Iran's oil buyer; 'not exempt'); Beijing told the US to 'act rationally' (25 Aug). Xi attended the BRICS summit in New Delhi (12–13 Sep; first India visit in seven years); the Declaration voiced 'deep concern' and 'maximum restraint' and did NOT name the US. Separately, Beijing's release of additional urea export quota pushed ME granular urea from ~$500 to ~$450/t — China is now the marginal price-setter for a Hormuz-sensitive input (DiscoveryAlert/Argus context). The Amodei 'AI slowdown' call and Fed-hike fear hit Asian chips 14 Sep (KOSPI −3.4%). (CNBC/NPR, Democracy Now, Wikipedia summit page, DiscoveryAlert — CONFIRMED sanctions; REPORTED urea mechanism)

Iran's formal 'complete closure' declaration (no nationality exceptions) ends the Iran-PERMITTED Chinese transits as policy -- the coordinated-passage instrument the graph tracked. Operationally unconfirmed (CENTCOM says transits continue). China is also the ~40% non-crisis leg of the aluminum demand-fear move (industrial softness) and the marginal-demand swing for Brent.

recent_signals.headline: **CHINESE CRUDE IMPORTS AT A ~10-YEAR LOW — THE DEMAND-SIDE WEIGHT THAT PRESSED BRENT -2% TO ~$93 ON 5 JUNE.** Chinese crude imports fell to a ~10-year low on soft refinery activity, the principal driver (with the lack of a US-Iran breakthrough) of Brent's -2.0% fall to $93.09 on 5 June, even as the renewed 5-6 June Gulf clashes kept Brent +~4% on the week. recent_signals.headline: **IRAN ALLOWED 30+ CHINESE SHIPS TO TRANSIT HORMUZ since May 13 night under 'Iranian management protocols'** (REPORTED — Fars/IRGC-Navy senior official primary; Iran state TV 'more than 30 ships'; Xinhua 'Iran begins letting some Chinese ships cross Strait of Hormuz' Chinese state amplification; Al Jazeera 'Trump, Xi discuss Strait of Hormuz as Chinese vessels transit key waterway'; CBS; Defense Post; Newsweek; Militarnyi; New Arab). Defense Post and Newsweek noted Iran has occasionally allowed Chinese ships even during the broader blockade because China is the largest buyer of Iranian oil. **The simultaneity with the Trump-Xi summit is the signal**: Xi's joint-statement line that he is 'interested in purchasing more American oil to reduce dependence on the Strait' co-exists with operational reliance on selective Iranian transit. **Trump immediately reversed post-summit ('decimation to be continued' Truth Social + Hannity 'not patient') and on May 16 sent Iran a new nuclear ultimatum letter** — the joint statement produced ZERO operational follow-through; China-as-HEU-custodian door is now operationally empty. **China silence post-summit (no MFA pushback on Trump's reversal)** — Beijing choosing not to engage Trump's contradictory rhetoric. The Aramco CEO Nasser benchmark ~30 vessels/day vs 140 pre-war is now partially explained: a portion is Iran-permitted Chinese transit, so non-Iranian non-Chinese transit is likely lower than headline figure. US markets sold off on the reversal: S&P -1.24%, NASDAQ -1.54%, Dow -1.07%, 10Y +14bp to 4.595%; tech sold off hard (Intel -6%, AMD -5.7%, Micron -6.6%, Nvidia -4.4%). Hang Seng -1.6% / Shanghai -1.0% — disappointment read absorbed but limited damage. USD/CNY 6.81 (+0.3% 1D); USD/CNY fix May 15 at 6.8415 vs Reuters 6.7976 = weaker-than-expected fix signaling tolerance for further yuan depreciation.

recent_signals.headline: **TRUMP-XI SUMMIT DAY 2: JOINT STATEMENT ISSUED — IRAN 'CAN NEVER HAVE A NUCLEAR WEAPON' + STRAIT OF HORMUZ 'MUST REMAIN OPEN'** (CONFIRMED multi-cluster primary: Times of Israel May 15 liveblog, CBS News, CNN Politics, China MFA official readout fmprc.gov.cn 2026-05-14, Trump Fox News interview, Al Jazeera, Asian Mirror). Both sides committed to a 'constructive China-U.S. relationship of strategic stability' framework guiding the next three years. **Xi additionally opposed 'the militarization of the Strait' and any effort to 'charge a toll' for its use**, and said China is interested in purchasing more American oil to reduce dependence on the Strait — operationally meaningful given >50% of Chinese energy transits Hormuz today. **The China MFA readout records that 'China values Iran's pledge not to pursue nuclear weapons while affirming its legitimate right to the peaceful use of nuclear energy'** = Iran's right-to-civilian-program escape valve preserved in language. China-as-HEU-custodian door is now soft-confirmed at rhetorical-alignment level; neither side announced an operational custodian framework; Xi has NOT publicly accepted a custodian role. **Trump's Fox News follow-on assertions (CLAIMED — single source, NOT in joint statement or MFA readout)**: Xi 'offered to broker peace with Iran,' assured 'won't provide military equipment to Iran,' committed to buying US soybeans/oil/LNG + 200 Boeing 737s. Analyst skepticism: China's existing soybean appetite is limited by cheap Brazilian alternatives (Reuters via People News Today). **Xinhua and Global Times carried the joint statement on China's terms — Beijing letting the meeting + strategic-stability framework speak rather than commenting on Trump's Fox News follow-on claims.** USD/CNY fix May 15 at 6.8415 vs Reuters estimate 6.7976 = weaker-than-expected fix signaling Beijing tolerance for further yuan depreciation; Shanghai Composite 4,121.01 (-1.4% 1D); Hang Seng 25,897.05 (-1.9% 1D) — Hang Seng Trump-Xi disappointment read (Foreign Policy: 'failed to secure major concessions'). China April exports +14.1% y/y record $359.4bn, imports +25.3%; lending rates unchanged 11th straight month. The 'China-as-HEU-custodian framework formally accepted by Iran + US within 30 days (by 2026-06-13)' trigger remains 'watching' — joint statement is rhetorical alignment, NOT operational custodian framework.

recent_signals.headline: China's operative position is a China-Pakistan joint call (17 Jul) for an immediate ceasefire and return to the June MoU, with Wang Yi warning the parties 'cannot fall at the last hurdle' and MFA spokesperson Mao Ning urging both to 'follow through on their memorandum of understanding... and avoid resorting to force.' Materially more important than the rhetoric: **China is quietly abandoning Iranian barrels.** Kpler puts China's Iranian crude imports at 556,000 bpd month-to-date July, the lowest since January 2023 and a 45%+ fall from just over 1m bpd earlier in the summer, while Shandong teapots bought 16-20.5m bbl of NON-SANCTIONED crude from Qatar, Iraq and the UAE — their largest such purchases of the war. Beijing calls for a ceasefire while its refiners de-risk away from Tehran. Separately China's Q2 GDP printed 4.3%, weakest since 2022, capping the oil premium from the demand side (Shanghai Composite -3.0% Friday). CONFIRMED.

Beijing continues to call for de-escalation while its refiners de-risk away from Tehran. **China and Pakistan jointly urged the US and Iran to resume talks.** On the commercial side the substitution the graph recorded on 19 July has **continued, not reversed**: Reuters (19 July) — *'Iran oil stuck at sea surges as China's teapots turn to rival Middle East supplies.'* Shandong refiners are still buying non-sanctioned Qatari, Iraqi and Emirati barrels while unsold Iranian crude accumulates in floating storage. Separately SCMP reports **China's June Gulf crude imports plunged** and Saudi imports sank to a **near eight-year low**, with China cutting refinery runs — Beijing is acting as a shock absorber by demand destruction as much as by substitution. **China is co-sponsoring the Russian UNSC counter-draft** condemning strikes on Iranian nuclear sites. ⚠️ COLLECTION GAP: no Xinhua or Global Times retrieval succeeded this cycle, so China's own messaging is unassessed — notable given the IRGC publicly thanked 'the Jordanian people' for targeting intelligence, possibly to counter reports that Russia and the PRC helped Iran target US assets. REPORTED.
